20 A progressive wave of frequency 1.5 kHz travels in a medium at a speed of 340 m s–1.
What is the minimum distance between two points on the wave that have a phase difference of
70?
A
4.4 cm
B
8.8 cm
C
18 cm
D
23 cm

hints: First find the wavelength from the given $1.5 \text{ kHz}$ frequency and $340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ speed using $v = f\lambda$.
Recall that a full wavelength $\lambda$ corresponds to a phase change of $360^{\circ}$ along a progressive wave.
Set up the fraction $x = (70/360) \times \lambda$ to get the minimum separation for $70^{\circ}$ and convert to $\text{cm}$.
walkthrough: Identify the data: $f = 1.5 \text{ kHz} = 1500 \text{ Hz}$ and $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Find the wavelength using $\lambda = v/f$, so $\lambda = 340/1500 \approx 0.227 \text{ m}$.
Use the phase-distance rule: phase difference $\phi = 360^{\circ} \times x/\lambda$, so $x = (\phi/360^{\circ}) \times \lambda$.
Convert to centimetres: $0.0441 \text{ m} \times 100 \approx 4.4 \text{ cm}$, which checks as much less than one wavelength. This is option A.

A.explanation: Correct - $70^{\circ}$ is $70/360$ of a wavelength, giving about $0.044 \text{ m} = 4.4 \text{ cm}$.

B.explanation: Incorrect - about twice the required distance, from using $140^{\circ}$ instead of $70^{\circ}$.

C.explanation: Incorrect - close to most of one wavelength, not the small fraction for $70^{\circ}$.

D.explanation: Incorrect - this is about one full wavelength of $22.7 \text{ cm}$, which is $360^{\circ}$ phase difference.
